essence: Treat the Item class as the existing data binding system
Consider property objects with their own events, via get/set, extending an events class
Let a POJO map property names to static values or live property objects for automatic render updates
Decide later how to prioritise data binding work

One item tool, not a tool per class: it takes a path and a method, and any class that extends Item has its public methods callable through it (instantiate, edit, call), so pages, tasks and sessions never need their own tools; the class definition is the documentation. Its first call returns tool instructions (the real API) so the always-loaded description stays small.

Later: a delta that edits part of a string (splice or replace) instead of rewriting a whole text property, so an agent refining a markdown card makes a small visible change rather than nuking and rewriting what the owner is reading. For now whole-string rewrites are fine, as long as they change only what's needed.
